[shr-00001] When searching for a target object and it is not immediately visible, prioritize exploring common storage locations such as shelves, tables, or countertops before investigating less likely locations such as basins or holders.
[shr-00002] When the target object is not found in common storage locations and the task remains incomplete, consider checking unlikely or non-storage locations such as toilets, basins, or holders, as the object may be placed there unexpectedly.
[shr-00003] When the target object is found in a common storage location, proceed directly to the destination object (e.g., toilet) without unnecessary intermediate actions or detours, as this improves task efficiency.
[shr-00005] When searching for a visible object like a soapbottle, prioritize checking countertops before opening cabinets, as countertops are more likely to hold such objects and avoid unnecessary actions.
[shr-00006] When a visible object like a soapbottle is not found on the countertop after an initial check, proceed to open cabinets in order, starting from the nearest or most likely ones, to minimize unnecessary actions.
[shr-00021] When a target object is found in a common storage location like a cabinet, immediately take the object before proceeding to the destination, to avoid unnecessary detours or closure of the source cabinet.
[shr-00024] When placing a clean cloth into a cabinet, prioritize an empty or less cluttered cabinet over a non-empty one to avoid clutter and ensure tidiness, as outlined in [vc-00023].
[shr-00042] When two instances of a visible object like a soapbar are found on a countertop or sinkbasin, proceed directly to the destination (e.g., garbagecan) after picking up each object to ensure efficiency and task completion.
[shr-00043] When one instance of a target object is found and placed in the destination and the task requires multiple instances, systematically open additional cabinets or re-check common storage locations to locate the remaining objects.
[shr-00046] When one instance of a target object is placed in the destination and the task requires multiple instances, avoid attempting to move the same object back to the same location unless explicitly instructed to reposition it. Instead, systematically search for the remaining objects as outlined in [shr-00043].
[shr-00048] When two instances of a visible object like a spraybottle are found on a sidetable (a common storage location), proceed directly to the destination (e.g., garbagecan) after picking up each object to ensure efficiency and task completion.
